claim: The footing domain is not uniformly the morphological word: a root plus a close/usually monosyllabic suffix forms one prosodic word, while prefixes and most disyllabic suffixes initiate a separate prosodic domain.

source_forms.domain_pattern: root + monomoraic/usually monosyllabic suffix = same p-word; prefix or most disyllabic suffix = separate p-word

normalized_environment: PWd domain depends on affix class/size
exceptions_or_counterexamples: The authors explicitly note exceptions among bimoraic suffixes and show that affix size is not the sole determinant for every suffix.
section: Abstract/Introduction; 4.5 Summary of stress in complex words; 5 Trochaic shortening

claim: Trochaic shortening avoids a foot composed of a long-vowel syllable followed by a light syllable: an underlying penultimate long vowel is normally shortened in unsuffixed words, while suffixation can alter the relevant footing domain and therefore the shortening outcome.

source_forms.repair: Vː -> V in unsuffixed H.L trochee

formal_environment: Vː in penultimate syllable before light final syllable
normalized_environment: avoid H.L trochee by long-vowel shortening; domain-sensitive under suffixation
exceptions_or_counterexamples: Suffixation yields variable or different outcomes because monosyllabic versus disyllabic suffixes differ in prosodic-word membership; loan examples also participate in the shortening pattern.

claim: In monomorphemic words, stress-disrupting 'diphthong formation' is found for /ai, au, ei, ou/ but not for /ae, ao, ea, eo, oa, ia, ie, iu, ua, uo/; the authors remain agnostic about whether the relevant sequences are one segment, tautosyllabic two-vowel sequences, or heterosyllabic.
normalized_environment: nonhigh+high VV subset triggers stress disruption; inventory empirically delimited
exceptions_or_counterexamples: No suitable lexical items were found for six sequences, so their status is explicitly unresolved; this inventory is narrower than some grammar-based diphthong lists.

claim: The productive ergative /-ina/ forms its own prosodic word, while ergative and denominal /-a/ show an idiosyncratic pre-stressing/foot-final requirement that becomes visible in VVa sequences.
exceptions_or_counterexamples: The /-a/ requirement is normally vacuous and becomes diagnostic only in a limited structural set; the authors therefore treat it as idiosyncratic rather than a general suffix rule.

claim: Underlying /i, u/ are often transcribed as [j, w] when unstressed, followed by a vowel, and not preceded by a consonant; after a stressed vowel they may instead be heard as [ij, uw]. The authors explicitly label the analysis speculative.
normalized_environment: unstressed high V -> glide tendency before V, conditioned by preceding segment/stress
exceptions_or_counterexamples: Classification of individual tokens as vowel versus glide is difficult and gradient; the authors call this section speculative and do not present the pattern as categorical.

claim: Mid /e, o/ are contrastive only in the root-initial syllable; in subsequent syllables they may surface only when preceded by a mid vowel in the privileged root-initial position, anchoring height harmony in the root-initial syllable.

source_forms.noninitial_condition: mid vowel licensed by preceding root-initial mid vowel

formal_environment: root-initial V versus subsequent V in verb
normalized_environment: mid-vowel contrast preserved root-initially; noninitial mid requires height harmony from initial trigger
exceptions_or_counterexamples: The abstract states the structural generalization but does not quantify lexical/loan/idiophone exceptions; those qualifications remain linked to the Hayes & Wilson corpus records rather than inferred here.
